name: P(death) severity scale
description: Continuous severity mapping from ordinal workplace injury categories to probability of death, grounded in AIS empirical mortality data (Baker 1974, NTDB) and corroborated by HSE appraisal costs.
rationale: The naive ordinal mapping (1,2,3,4) assumes equal spacing. AIS mortality data shows approximately geometric spacing — each level represents a 4-6x increase in P(death). P(death) is bounded [0,1], directly interpretable, and empirically grounded.
sif_threshold_rationale: Serious injury spans AIS 3-4 (3-16% mortality). A midpoint of 10% aligns with HSE 'specified injury' category. P(SIF) = P(death >= 0.10).

categories.label: no_injury
categories.description: No anatomical injury, no treatment needed

categories.label: first_aid
categories.description: Minor: abrasions, superficial lacerations, minor sprains. AIS 1 mortality ~0.1%

categories.label: medical_treatment
categories.description: Moderate: simple fractures, lacerations needing sutures, undisplaced fractures. AIS 2 mortality ~0.5%

categories.label: serious_injury
categories.description: Serious/severe: displaced fractures, open fractures, organ damage, amputations. AIS 3 mortality ~3%, AIS 4 ~16%. Midpoint ~10%

categories.label: fatality
categories.description: Critical/unsurvivable: death. AIS 5 mortality ~64%, AIS 6 ~75-100% (defined as unsurvivable)

sources.ais_mortality: Baker SP et al. (1974). The Injury Severity Score. J Trauma 14(3):187-196
sources.ntdb: National Trauma Data Bank. AIS-6 survival ~25% (Surviving AIS-6, J Surgical Research 2021)
